reason: The Cluster-tier definition prescribes P/D disaggregation as the response to traffic growth, but the chapter's own 10x worked example responds to traffic growth with data-parallel replication, not P/D disaggregation. The definition over-specifies one mechanism and is inconsistent with the worked example.
evidence: chapter-13.md §1 item 3: 'Required when a model exceeds a node's memory (so it must be split per Ch10) or when traffic outgrows one host (so P/D disaggregation per Ch11 applies).' chapter-13.md §13.3: 'Response: replicate the model across multiple servers (data parallelism at the serving layer — run N identical 8xH100 hosts behind a load balancer).' The 10x example never invokes P/D disaggregation.
fix_instruction: File design/manuscript/chapter-13/chapter-13.md, §1 item 3 (Cluster tier). Anchor: 'or when traffic outgrows one host (so P/D disaggregation per Ch11 applies).' Replace 'when traffic outgrows one host (so P/D disaggregation per Ch11 applies)' with 'when traffic outgrows one host (requiring multi-host scaling: data-parallel replication, P/D disaggregation, or both — Ch 11)' so the definition matches the §13.3 DP worked example and does not imply P/D disaggregation is the only/default response.
